verdicts.note: (not flagged verify) IMSLP: '7 Artistic-Instructive Pieces for Violin and Piano', Op. 54, composed 1911, publ. Muzgiz 1926 / Sovetsky Kompozitor 1961; 7 pieces in 2 books (Prelude, Pastoral, Esquisse, Minuet, Melodie, Pres du ruisseau, Humoresque); violin part in 1st-3rd position. IMSLP's note on Op. 45 calls Op. 54 the 'real intermediate level' set, so the queued levels look inverted (Op. 54 = 1-2, Op. 45 = 2-3).

(not flagged verify) IMSLP: '12 Pieces faciles pour violon et piano', Op. 45, Jurgenson 1910 (Prelude, Valse, Romance, Chanson populaire, Caprice, Etude, Air, Impromptu, Mazurka, Intermezzo, Nocturne, Scherzo). IMSLP note: 'in spite of the title most of these pieces are far from easy, requiring up to 5th position and difficult intervals' - queued level 1 is probably too low (suggest 2-3).

Exists as titled: IMSLP '8 Pieces (Duos) for violin and cello, Op. 39' (Huit Morceaux (Duos) pour Violon et Violoncelle), 1909, Jurgenson (plates 33167-33174), reprint Forberg; c. 15 min; movements Prelude, Gavotte, Berceuse, Canzonetta, Intermezzo, Impromptu, Scherzo, Etude. Wikipedia lists it as '8 Duets for Violin and Cello, Op. 39 (1909)'. 'cello' was only unsupported because the IMSLP title omits it.

(not flagged verify) IMSLP: Violin Concerto Op. 100 in G minor, alt. title 'Concert-Allegro', one movement, 1956, completed/orchestrated by Boris Lyatoshinsky; violin & piano edition ed. Lyatoshinsky and Mostras, Muzgiz 1960 (plate 28487). Wikipedia: 'Concerto for violin and orchestra (Concerto-Allegro) in G minor, Op. 100 (1956)'. Recorded by Yuko Nishino / Yondani Butt / Philharmonia Orchestra (2002).

gaps.note: OPTIONAL (published, no recording found - not on the Toccata Hartmann CD). Not the same piece as the original Romance in D major, Op. 3 (id 966). Second source: Wikipedia's Glière article also notes a violin/piano arrangement of Op. 47.
